HOURS.title: What the pay has to cover: Tijuana, San Diego, Denver
HOURS.question: The same household needs food, rent and bus rides. How much of a month's pay does that take on each side of the wall, and in Denver, at the minimum wage and below it?
HOURS.notice: Start at the minimum wage, then switch Tijuana to what many workers really earn. In Baja California almost a third earn one minimum wage or less, and nearly a third more don't report their pay. Measured in hours and shares of pay, there is no exchange rate to argue about. The rent is the open question: no source yet gives a colonia rent, so you set it.
HOURS.yourCall: At the pay you chose, how many earners does the Tijuana household need? Who in the family would that be, and what would they stop doing?

pays.label: The minimum wage (one full-time earner)
pays.note: 440.87 pesos a day (2026), about 13,400 a month on a 48-hour week (our arithmetic; a daily wage also pays the rest day).

pays.label: Set it yourself
pays.note: In Baja California, 31.5% of workers earned up to one minimum wage and 30.4% did not report their pay (Q2 2025). No source gives what a vendor earns; this starts at half the minimum. Set your own and say so.
